A_target.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Consistent|consistent]] [[Definition:Theory (Logic)|theory]] of [[Definition:First-Order Logic|first-order logic]].
Then $T$ has a [[Definition:Model (Logic)|model]].

B_source.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Consistent|consistent]] [[Definition:Theory (Logic)|theory]].
If $T$ is [[Definition:Complete Theory|complete]] and has [[Definition:Henkin Witness|witnesses]] for all existential sentences, then the [[Definition:Term Model|term model]] of closed terms modulo provable equality is a model of $T$.

substitutions.the syntactic objects used as elements: closed terms of the extended language, modulo provable equality
substitutions.the extension step: adding a constant witnessing each existential statement
substitutions.the maximality step: extending to a complete consistent theory deciding every sentence

derived.the structure read off the syntax: the term model, whose relations are given by provability
derived.the truth lemma: a sentence holds in the term model exactly when the extended theory proves it

object_map.reformulation: Read the model off the syntax itself, after enriching the theory enough that the syntax names every needed element.

validity_conditions: Adding witness constants preserves consistency, since a proof of contradiction from the extension would translate back into one from the original theory.
Maximality is obtained by Zorn's lemma or by enumerating sentences, and it makes the term model well defined by deciding every atomic statement.
Provable equality must be quotiented out, or terms naming the same element would give distinct elements and the equality axioms would fail.
proof_plan:
Add new constants $c_\phi$ and axioms $\exists x \, \map \phi x \to \map \phi {c_\phi}$ for every formula $\phi$.
Each extension preserves [[Definition:Consistent|consistency]].
By [[Lindenbaum's Lemma]], extend to a [[Definition:Complete Theory|complete]] consistent theory $T^*$ deciding every sentence.

Let $M$ be the set of closed terms modulo:
:$s \sim t \iff T^* \vdash s = t$
Interpret function and relation symbols by their action on representatives, which is [[Definition:Well-Defined Mapping|well-defined]] by the equality axioms.

By [[Principle of Structural Induction|induction]] on formulas, using the witnesses for the existential case:
:$M \models \phi \iff T^* \vdash \phi$
This is the [[Definition:Truth Lemma|truth lemma]].
Hence $M \models T$.
{{qed}}
